advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove or replace the tautological `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` guards on publish/github_release/mcp_registry (dispatch is the only trigger; rely on the needs: authorize chain).
evidence: release.yml:40-46 `on:` declares only `workflow_dispatch` (no `push`)
release.yml:280 `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` (publish)
release.yml:317 `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` (github_release)
release.yml:403 `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` (mcp_registry)
advisory.finding: After removing the `push: tags: v*` trigger, `workflow_dispatch` is the workflow's ONLY trigger, so the `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` guards on the publish, github_release, and mcp_registry jobs are tautological (always true). The real authorization gate is the `needs:` chain up to `authorize`; these `if:` lines are dead conditions that imply a dry-run/non-dispatch path that no longer exists.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make check_env_protection fail closed when branch_policies is None but deployment_branch_policy uses custom branch policies (do not silently skip the main-only assertion).
evidence: scripts/release_guards.py:111-115 only asserts `deployment_branch_policy` is not null (does not inspect which branches)
scripts/release_guards.py:117-123 `if branch_policies is not None:` — the exactly-{main} check is skipped entirely when None

test coverage passes branch_policies in every non-None case (test_release_guards.py test_env_preflight_branch_policy_null_fails calls with None but relies on the null deployment_branch_policy, not the branch list)
advisory.finding: `check_env_protection` only performs the main-only branch-policy assertion when `branch_policies is not None`; when called with `branch_policies=None` it can return `[]` (compliant) for an environment whose `deployment_branch_policy` is non-null but allows arbitrary custom branches. The helper's docstring says it verifies the environment 'restricts deploys to main', but that guarantee is conditional on the second argument being supplied.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Catch git errors in the ancestry CLI path and surface them as a `release_guards:` failure string rather than an uncaught CalledProcessError traceback.
evidence: scripts/release_guards.py:87-92 raises CalledProcessError on any returncode not in {0,1}
scripts/release_guards.py:134-137 `_cmd_ancestry` calls is_ancestor with no try/except
module docstring (scripts/release_guards.py:29-31) states main 'prints failures to stderr and exits 0 (ok) / 1 (failure)'
advisory.finding: `is_ancestor` raises an uncaught `subprocess.CalledProcessError` for any git exit status other than 0/1 (e.g., an unknown/unfetched ref, returncode 128). `_cmd_ancestry` and `main` do not catch it, so the ancestry CLI path emits a raw Python traceback and a non-standard exit code instead of the clean `release_guards: ...` stderr line + exit 1 that the module's contract describes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add CLI (rg.main) smoke tests for the `env-preflight` and `ancestry` subcommands asserting exit 0 on compliant inputs and exit 1 on a drift/non-ancestor, driving them through the same `--response/--branch-policies/--sha/--ref` argument wiring the workflow uses.
evidence: release.yml line 100-101: `python scripts/release_guards.py env-preflight --response env.json --branch-policies branch-policies.json`
release.yml line 90: `python scripts/release_guards.py ancestry --sha "$SHA" --ref origin/main`

test_release_guards.py:218 `def test_cli_version_lockstep_exit_codes` is the only rg.main() invocation — no CLI test exercises the `env-preflight` or `ancestry` subcommands (`_cmd_env_preflight`/`_cmd_ancestry`), which are the only production entrypoints for those guards
advisory.finding: The env-preflight and ancestry CLI subcommands — the SOLE way the release workflow invokes these guards (`python scripts/release_guards.py env-preflight --response env.json --branch-policies branch-policies.json` and `... ancestry --sha ... --ref origin/main`) — have no test. Only `_cmd_version_lockstep` has a CLI smoke test (test_cli_version_lockstep_exit_codes). A regression in the env-preflight/ancestry argument wiring, file-read, or JSON parsing (e.g. a renamed/swapped flag, or failing to pass branch-policies) would pass the whole suite yet break the release at publish time.
scenarios: A refactor renames --branch-policies or swaps _cmd_env_preflight's --response/--branch-policies file reads; pure-helper tests stay green but the workflow guard silently mis-parses or crashes at release time
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror test_cli_version_lockstep_exit_codes: write env.json + branch-policies.json fixtures to tmp_path and assert rg.main(["env-preflight", "--response", ..., "--branch-policies", ...]) returns 0 for _env_ok()/_policies_main() and 1 for a cleared reviewer/non-main policy; for ancestry, drive rg.main(["ancestry", "--sha", repo['C'], "--ref", "main"]) with cwd via monkeypatch.chdir(repo['dir']).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an env-preflight test with deployment_branch_policy=None AND a real branch-policies dict (as the CLI always supplies) asserting the null-policy failure is still reported.
evidence: test_release_guards.py:200-201 `env["deployment_branch_policy"] = None` then `rg.check_env_protection(env, None)` — second arg is None
release.yml:100-101 always passes `--branch-policies branch-policies.json`, so _cmd_env_preflight always calls check_env_protection with a non-None dict

release_guards.py:111 the `deployment_branch_policy is null` failure and release_guards.py:117 the branch_policies check are independent branches; the null case is never exercised alongside a real branch_policies dict as production does
advisory.finding: The env-preflight test for a null deployment_branch_policy (test_env_preflight_branch_policy_null_fails) passes branch_policies=None, but the production CLI (_cmd_env_preflight, driven by the workflow) ALWAYS supplies a real branch-policies dict. The production-representative combination — deployment_branch_policy null WHILE a branch-policies dict is present — is not exercised, leaving the actual drift shape the workflow feeds in untested.
scenarios: An environment reports deployment_branch_policy: null but the deployment-branch-policies endpoint returns {main}; the test never covers this real combination
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: env = _env_ok(); env["deployment_branch_policy"] = None; fails = rg.check_env_protection(env, _policies_main()); assert any("branch" in f.lower() for f in fails).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate `inputs.version` against a strict semver pattern (in release_guards.py version-lockstep and/or before use) and stop interpolating `${version}` into the `python3 -c` string — pass it via argv/env (e.g. `sys.argv[1]` or `os.environ`) instead of source interpolation.
evidence: release.yml:452 `VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}` then release.yml:454 `version="${VERSION}"`

release.yml:456 `curl -fsS "..." | python3 -c "import json,sys; v='${version}'; d=json.load(sys.stdin); ..."` — `${version}` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted Python source literal, so a value containing `'` breaks out into executable Python

The diff re-keys the taint source from `TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}` / `version="${TAG#v}"` to `VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}` / `version="${VERSION}"`, moving to a more directly attacker-controlled dispatch input

scripts/release_guards.py:37-68 `check_version_lockstep` compares only via `!=` string equality; no regex/semver validation of the version anywhere (search for `re.match` in release_guards.py returned no matches)

REACHABILITY (evidence for scoring): mcp_registry is a `needs:` descendant of build->authorize, so version-lockstep runs first; the injected value must therefore also equal pyproject.toml `[project].version` and server.json versions. Because lockstep is pure string equality, a malformed/payload version landed in those files would pass lockstep and reach the sink unescaped. Exploitation requires landing the payload through Gerrit review (mitigation), and dispatch requires repo write — this is a defense-in-depth taint-to-sink gap, not a directly-unauthenticated exploit.
advisory.finding: The attacker-influenceable `workflow_dispatch` input `inputs.version` flows unvalidated into a `python3 -c` program string in the mcp_registry job (`v='${version}'`), a code-execution sink; neither the workflow nor release_guards.py validates the version as a strict semver, and the version-lockstep guard uses only raw string equality (no format check), so a version string is never sanitized before reaching the sink.
scenarios: A version string containing a single quote or Python code (e.g. carried in a reviewed pyproject.toml bump) is interpolated into the `python3 -c` literal on release.yml:456 and executed on the OIDC-privileged mcp_registry runner.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a semver format check to `check_version_lockstep` (reject any version not matching `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+...$`) and rewrite release.yml:456 to pass the version via the environment (`import os; v=os.environ['VERSION']`) rather than shell-interpolating it into the `-c` program text.
